MCC MegaCell Compiler Tutorial

About this Document

This chapter provides an overview of the Micro Magic Tools MegaCell Compiler Tutorial:

  • Objectives on this page.
    •

  • Getting set up on page "Getting set up".
    •

Objectives

This tutorial is a intended to be a step-by-step introductory training in the use of the Micro Magic Tools (TM) Mega Cell Compiler (MCC). By following the steps in this tutorial, you will learn how to run MCC, and how to use MCC to optimize your memory designs. Once you are familiar with MCC, refer to the Micro Magic Tools MCC User Guide for more detailed information about the tool and it's options.

Audience - MCC

This document is designed for physical chip designers, specifically custom memory designers. It assumes that you have a strong foundation in chip layout and development, and memory design. This document also assumes that you are familiar with the following programming languages and operating systems:Tcl/Tk, and UNIX or Linux.

Organization

This tutorial is divided into parts. Each part leads you through a different aspect of the Micro Magic Tools MegaCell Compiler.

This document contains the following parts:

  • Preface, "About This Document" (this chapter), provides a brief description of the content and organization of this document.
    •

  • Part 1, "Mega Cell Compiler (MCC) Tutorial", gives a brief overview of what you can accomplish using MCC, and the requirements necessary for running the program.

  • Part 2, "Running MCC", provides instructions on setting up and running MCC, and writing MCC control programs. It goes through each section of the MCC Control Program, as well as covering the MC Build and MC What commands.
    •

  • Part 3, "MC Critical Path Analysis", covers how to use MCC to extract a critical path for a memory. It also presents instructions for viewing the results of SPICE simulation of the critical path.
    •

  • Part 4, "Netlisting", introduces the MCC capability to extract a SPICE or Verilog netlist directly from the megacell layout.

Chapter Organization

Each part contains descriptions of the commands and methodology necessary to create memories using MCC, with step-by-step, illustrative examples describing the usage of commands and procedures.

Documentation Conventions

General Conventions

This guide uses the following text conventions:

  • Statements, commands, command output, filenames, directory names, and configurations are shown in a boldface, fixed-width font. The following example shows a full path name:
    •  
    ~/mmi_private/max/.maxrc

  • In examples, text that you type literally is shown in bold. In the following example, you type the word max:
    •  
    To launch max, type max

  • Menus, menu options, and pop-up menus are generally shown in a boldface, sans serif font. For example:
    •  
    Select Save As from the File Menu.

Conventions for Software Commands and Statements

When describing the Micro Magic Tools (TM) software, this guide uses the following type and presentation conventions:

  • Statement or command names that you type literally are shown nonitalicized. In the following example, the statement name is set MC(default_generator):
    •  
    set MC(default_generator) sram

  • Variables for which you substitute appropriate values, are shown in itallics. Optional commands within a string of code are often enclosed within square brackets ([ ]). Variables are enclosed within angle brackets (<>). When you type the setMACRO statement, you substitute a value for name, row1 and row2. CELL is an optional command. 
    • set MACRO(<name>){[CELL]<row1><row2>...}

Conventions for Mousing

Throughout this document, we assume you are using a 3-button mouse. When we refer to using the mouse, the following settings apply:

  • Mouse-Button-1, or Button-1, refers to the left-most button (index finger) when you are using a right-handed mouse.

  • Mouse-Button-2, or Button-2, refers to the middle, or center button (middle finger).
    •

  • Mouse-Button-3, or Button-3, refers to the right-most button (ring finger) when using a right-handed mouse.

Reverse these settings if you are using a left-handed mouse, using your mouse control program, so that you click Button-1 with your index finger, Button-2 with your middle finger, and Button-3 with your ring finger.

  • "Click" means to depress the designated mouse button once.
    •

  • "Double-click" means to depress the designated mouse button twice, quickly.
    •

  • "Drag" means to depress and hold down the designated mouse button while moving the mouse.
    •

Getting set up

MCC runs from within the Micro Magic Tools MAX Layout Editor.

First, ensure that the Micro Magic Tools software has been installed, and that you have MAX and MCC installed.

If you have an MCC license (max_mcc), you need to enable the MCC menu commands with the command mc_init. Typically, you add this command to the system .maxrc file ($MMI_TOOLS/../mmi_local/max/.maxrc) so everyone has access to it. If only specific users run MCC, they can add it to their own .maxrc files (~/mmi_private/max/.maxrc).

The mc_init command adds the MCC commands to the Tool menu in MAX Layout Editor. For clarity, all of the MCC commands are prefixed by the string MC. When a user attempts to execute any one of these commands, MAX checks that a valid MCC license is available, and if so, checks out that license for the remainder of the MAX session. Note that the mc_init command by itself does not check out an MCC license.
